Chinese astronomers have detected an unusual radio signal apparently originating from the K2-155 star system, approximately 238 light-years from Earth, according to WION.

The signal exhibits characteristics that scientists look for when searching for extraterrestrial technology. However, researchers have not confirmed that it originated from an alien civilisation.

Designated NBS 260108, the signal was detected by China's Five-hundred-metre Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope (FAST) during an analysis of observations of 33 planetary systems conducted in 2021.

It was characterised by an exceptionally narrow frequency range and a gradual shift in frequency.

Such properties can be associated with artificial transmitters because natural cosmic processes generally do not produce radio signals with these characteristics.

The signal was also detected in only one of the telescope's 19 beams, the one directed towards K2-155.

The star system contains three super-Earth planets, which are larger than Earth. One of them, K2-155d, completes an orbit every 40.7 days and lies near a region where liquid water might potentially exist.

This makes the system an attractive target in the search for extraterrestrial life.

Nevertheless, scientists remain cautious about interpreting the discovery.

Further analysis identified similar radio signals during observations of three other stars, strengthening the possibility that the source was terrestrial radio interference or equipment belonging to the telescope itself.

Researchers plan to examine additional recordings from all 19 beams to establish the signal's origin.

For now, the observation has not been accepted as confirmed evidence of extraterrestrial technology. | BGNES
